Subject: Planned maintenance: East Asia host recycling & driver refresh - Jun 21 2026

Hi Kenji and team,

I wanted to give you an early heads-up about a scheduled maintenance activity we will perform in the East Asia inference fleet (ap-east1) on Jun 21, 2026. This is a rolling host-recycle combined with NIC/driver refreshs that helps keep driver/kernel stacks aligned with our latest runtime optimizations.

Window: 2026-06-21 03:00–07:00 UTC (staggered across availability zones)
Expected customer-visible impact: brief single-digit-second session drains for in-flight requests while a host is drained; short transient latency increases (we expect <= 10ms P95 bump for active connections). No planned data-plane outages; inference routing will failover to healthy hosts.

Key notes:
- We will drain hosts one at a time per AZ and perform a driver/firmware refresh; each host is expected back online within ~10 minutes.
- KV cache warmup: we will preserve prefix/KV caches where possible; warmup will be automatic but some cold-start token overhead may occur for sessions routed to freshly recycled hosts.
- Fallbacks: if you prefer to avoid any risk of latency bump, we can route your traffic to a pinned dedicated pool for the window (please reply if you want a temporary exclusion).
- For customers with strict egress IP allowlists, see the attached host list (east-asia-hostlist-20260621.csv) and the status page link below.

Attachments: maintenance-checklist.pdf (high-level runbook), east-asia-hostlist-20260621.csv (egress IPs & host IDs)

If you have any blackout constraints or need us to coordinate a different window, please reply with the constraint and a contact who we should loop into the escalation channel.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes

Cc-ing for visibility — notes you can forward to Kenji:

Kenji — quick technical clarifications from SRE:
- KV cache: warm KV entries are preserved for hosts that are re-attached to the pool. During drain we do a best-effort KV snapshot/attach where supported; however, clients routed to a freshly recycled host may see higher token decode times until the KV warms. In practice we've seen additional token overhead equivalent to 5–15ms for the first few requests for a freshly-warmed session.
- Expected latency delta: we project a <=10ms P95 increase on routed requests during the 1–2 minute handover window per host. The longer ~10min host maintenance time is driven by driver reload, microcode verification, and health-check cycles; active sessions are drained first.
- Egress IPs: the attached CSV lists host IPs and ranges. There are no changes to the stable NAT egress blocks for this activity; if you maintain an allowlist against individual host IPs, please use the CSV. If you use our published egress ranges (recommended), there are no changes.
- Pinned pool pricing: routing to a temporary pinned pool is possible; pricing depends on committed vGPU-minutes and model footprint — sales can share a short estimate.

I've updated the maintenance-checklist.pdf to include the KV-preservation caveat and the hostlist CSV.

-- Marcus Lin
SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

- Latency: projected <=10ms P95 bump during per-host handover. No broad outages expected.
- Egress IPs: no change to published NAT egress ranges; use attached CSV only if you pin against individual host IPs.

Options for AI Solutions Japan:
1) Default: accept rolling drains as scheduled — no change required from you.
2) Pinned exclusion: we can route your production traffic to a pinned pool for the 4-hour window (extra cost applies). Reply with the desired option and a billing contact if you select this.
3) Custom window: if this window conflicts with a blackout, tell us a preferred alternative window within the next 48 hours and we will evaluate.
